hyps.why: Edge 4 takes its input from node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so the conv adds nothing.
Edge 2 also starts at node 1, which receives nothing when edge 0 is none.
Node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 4 is inert.
Node 1 is dead, so edge 2 carries nothing.
A skip from a dead node adds no useful path.
Filling an empty direct edge with a conv gains more than replacing an existing op.
Any parametric direct path beats none.
Adding the direct shortcut where none existed gives a large gain.
Enabling the output edge of node 2 with a conv gains more than replacing an existing op.
Edge 0 gates node 1 and its two downstream edges, so enabling it with a conv helps a lot.
